subtitle: Exile, Vision, and the Birth of the Ras Lila

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot in twilight, king half in shadow, temple silhouette behind
panels.action: King Bhagya Chandra stands in exile robes beneath a darkening sky, hands folded, as a distant vision of dancers circling a faint Govindaji idol shimmers behind him like a mirage over the hills of Manipur.

dialogue.text: In an age of exile and war, King Bhagya Chandra of Manipur dreamed a dance—and turned a wounded kingdom into a moving circle around Govindaji.

i18n.hi: जंगल-वनवास और जंग के दौर में, मणिपुर के राजा भाग्यचन्द्र ने एक नृत्य का सपना देखा—और टूटी रियासत को गोविंदजी के चारों तरफ घूमती मण्डली बना दिया।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye of Imphal valley with fort and surrounding hills
panels.action: From high above the Imphal valley, the palace of Kangla rises amid mist and winding rivers, as King Bhagya Chandra, still young, stands on the rampart looking over his small but strategic kingdom at the eastern frontier.

dialogue.text: Mid-eighteenth century. Manipur is a hill-ringed valley between Burma and Assam, its kings balancing tribute, raids and trade along the eastern frontier of the subcontinent.

i18n.hi: अठारहवीं सदी का बीच। मणिपुर, पहाड़ियों से घिरी घाटी, बर्मा और असम के बीच, जहाँ राजा पूर्वी सरहद पर नजराने, लूट और व्यापार का संतुलन साधते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on king’s face, brows furrowed, listening to a courtier’s unseen report
panels.action: King Bhagya Chandra stands in his wooden hall, bare-chested with a royal shawl, face tense as he turns toward an unseen messenger, while a map of Manipur and Burma lies unrolled beside him on a low table.

dialogue.text: The chronicles call him Ching-Thang Khomba, later remembered as Bhagya Chandra. His throne stands between Ahom Assam to the west and the expanding Burmese kingdom to the east.

i18n.hi: इतिहास उसे चिंगथांग खोंबा कहता है, बाद में भाग्यचन्द्र के नाम से याद करता है। उसका तख्त, पश्चिम में अहोम असम और पूर्व में फैलते बर्मी साम्राज्य के बीच खड़ा है।

panels.shot: wide shot of palace courtyard with soldiers scattering as flames rise in distance
panels.action: In a night scene, Bhagya Chandra turns sharply as orange light flares beyond the palace walls, Manipuri soldiers rushing to arms while distant structures burn on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Conflict with Burma intensifies. Raids, counter-raids, shifting alliances. At one point, the Manipur court is broken and the king is driven from his own valley.

i18n.hi: बर्मा से टकराव भड़क उठता है। हमले, पलट-हमले, बदलते दोस्त-दुश्मन। एक वक्त ऐसा आता है जब दरबार टूट जाता है और राजा अपनी ही घाटी से खदेड़ दिया जाता है।

panels.shot: long shot of a small royal group on the move through forested hills
panels.action: Bhagya Chandra, dressed more like a traveler than a crowned king, rides or walks along a narrow forest path with a few attendants, the dense hills around them hinting at the long road toward Assam.

dialogue.text: The court chronicle records exile. The king leaves his homeland, seeking safety and allies in the west, toward the Ahom kingdom of Assam.

i18n.hi: दरबारी बखान में वनवास दर्ज है। राजा अपना देस छोड़ता है, पश्चिम की ओर, अहोम असम की तरफ, पनाह और साथी तलाशने निकल पड़ता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ahom court hall in Gargaon, with Bhagya Chandra standing before the throne
panels.action: In an Ahom palace hall with carved pillars and Assamese nobles seated in rows, Bhagya Chandra stands respectfully before the Ahom king, hands joined, while armored Ahom guards watch from the sides.

dialogue.text: In Assam, he turns from fugitive to guest. The Ahom court weighs his plea: help him regain Manipur, and a buffer against Burma will be restored.

i18n.hi: असम में भगोड़ा मेहमान बन जाता है। अहोम दरबार उसकी गुहार तौलता है: मणिपुर वापस दिलाओ, तो बर्मा के खिलाफ ढाल भी मिल जाएगी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Bhagya Chandra at night, seated cross-legged, eyes closed in devotion
panels.action: At night in a modest Assamese chamber, Bhagya Chandra sits cross-legged before a small oil lamp and a simple image of Krishna, eyes closed, palms pressed together in intense prayer.

dialogue.text: By this time, Vaishnava devotion, shaped by Gaudiya bhakti, has reached Manipur. In exile, Bhagya Chandra turns inward, deepening his worship of Krishna.

i18n.hi: तब तक गौड़ीय भक्ती से छनकर आई वैष्णव भक्ति मणिपुर पहुँच चुकी थी। वनवास में भाग्यचन्द्र भीतर मुड़ता है, कृष्ण-भक्ति और गहरी हो जाती है।

panels.shot: dreamlike wide shot of a moonlit field where Krishna and gopis dance in a circle
panels.action: In a luminous, otherworldly scene, a blue-hued Krishna plays the flute at the center as gopis in Manipuri-style skirts move in a graceful circle under the moon, while a translucent image of Bhagya Chandra watches in awe.

dialogue.text: Court tradition says that in this time he dreams Krishna. Not a simple vision, but a circle of dancers around the dark cowherd, the Ras, under a moon that feels like home.

i18n.hi: दरबारी परम्परा कहती है, इन्हीं दिनों उसे कृष्ण का सपना आता है। सिर्फ झलक नहीं, एक गोल घेरा—अँधेरे गोपाल के चारों ओर नृत्य करते गोपी-गोपाल, चाँदनी में रस का मैदान, जो घर सा लगने लगता है।

panels.shot: close-up on Bhagya Chandra waking, sweat on his brow, eyes bright with resolve
panels.action: Bhagya Chandra jolts awake on a simple bed, the faint light of dawn entering the room, his expression a mix of wonder and fierce determination as he looks toward the east.

dialogue.speaker: king_bhagya_chandra
dialogue.text: If I return, Govindaji will stand in Manipur, and the Ras will be his worship.

i18n.hi: यदि मैं लौटा, तो गोविंदजी मणिपुर में विराजेंगे, और रस ही उनकी पूजा होगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Manipuri and Ahom forces marching together through a valley
panels.action: Bhagya Chandra rides at the head of a joint Ahom-Manipuri force, Ahom soldiers in distinctive helmets alongside Manipuri warriors, as they move through a river valley toward the misty hills of Manipur.

dialogue.text: The chronicles note Ahom help. With Assamese support, the exiled king leads forces back through the passes, aiming to reclaim the Imphal valley from Burmese-backed rivals.

i18n.hi: इतिहास अहोम मदद दर्ज करता है। असमी सेना की सहारा लेकर वनवासी राजा, पहाड़ी दर्रों से वापस कूच करता है, इम्फाल घाटी को बर्मी समर्थक दुश्मनों से छीनने के लिए।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of battle lines facing each other on a plain, without gore
panels.action: Two ordered lines of warriors face each other on a plain, shields raised and spears ready, as Bhagya Chandra on horseback signals with his arm, clouds of dust rising between the opposing sides.

dialogue.text: There are clashes, losses, negotiations. The war is hard, but by the later 1760s, his position in Manipur is restored. Exile ends; rule resumes.

i18n.hi: टक्करें होती हैं, जानें जाती हैं, सुलहें भी होती हैं। जंग मुश्किल है, पर सत्रह सौ साठ के बाद तक मणिपुर में उसका राज फिर जम जाता है। वनवास खत्म; शासन लौट आता है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of the king entering Kangla fort, people bowing on either side
panels.action: Bhagya Chandra strides through the gate of Kangla fort, elders and commoners alike bowing, some with folded hands, others pressing their heads to the ground as the king’s face shows both relief and gravity.

dialogue.text: But the valley he returns to is not the same. War has scattered families, shaken old rituals, and left a question: what now binds Manipur together?

i18n.hi: पर घाटी अब पहले जैसी नहीं। जंग ने खानदान बिखेर दिए, पुरानी रस्में हिला दीं, और एक सवाल छोड़ दिया: अब मणिपुर को क्या चीज़ जोड़ेगी?

panels.shot: wide shot of a sacred grove where traditional Lai Haraoba is being performed
panels.action: In a green sacred grove, traditional priests and dancers perform Lai Haraoba, moving in curved patterns around a small shrine, while Bhagya Chandra watches from the shade, thoughtful and attentive.

dialogue.text: For centuries, Lai Haraoba had told the valley’s old stories—of deities, creation, and the land itself. Now Vaishnava bhakti presses in, asking for new forms of devotion.

i18n.hi: सदियों से लाई हराओबा घाटी की पुरानी गाथाएँ सुनाता था—देवताओं, सृष्टि और धरती की कहानियाँ। अब वैष्णव भक्ति दस्तक देती है, नई भक्ति-रूपों की माँग करती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king in council with Brahmanas, gurus, and traditional priests
panels.action: Inside a wooden hall, Bhagya Chandra sits with Vaishnava gurus, Brahmanas, and traditional Maibas and Maibis, his hands outstretched as if balancing two sides, while scrolls and drums lie between them.

dialogue.text: Historians like Moirangthem Kirti Singh describe a kingdom negotiating change. The king stands at the meeting point of Gaudiya Vaishnavism and older Meitei ritual life.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार मोइरंगथेम किर्ति सिंह जैसे लोग बताते हैं कि यह रियासत बदलाव से जूझ रही थी। राजा गौड़ीय वैष्णव परम्परा और पुरानी मैतेई रस्म-रिवाजों के संगम पर खड़ा है।

panels.shot: mid-shot of the king overseeing artisans carving an image of Krishna
panels.action: Bhagya Chandra watches closely as artisans carve a graceful Krishna idol from wood, one craftsman chiseling the flute, another shaping the crown, while the king’s gaze is focused and reverent.

dialogue.text: The chronicles credit him with installing Govindaji, a Krishna image, as Manipur’s royal deity. For the king, this is both devotion and statecraft—a divine center for a fragmented land.

i18n.hi: इतिहास लिखता है कि उसने गोविंदजी, कृष्ण विग्रह, को मणिपुर का राज-देवता बनाकर स्थापित किया। उसके लिए यह भक्ति भी है और राजनीति भी—टूटी धरती के लिए एक दिव्य केन्द्र।

panels.shot: wide shot of a temple courtyard with Govindaji idol raised on a pedestal
panels.action: In a new temple courtyard, the freshly carved Govindaji idol is lifted onto a pedestal with ropes and careful hands, as Bhagya Chandra stands below with folded hands among a gathered crowd.

dialogue.speaker: king_bhagya_chandra
dialogue.text: From this day, our kingdom circles his feet, not my throne.

i18n.hi: आज से हमारा राज्य उसके चरणों की परिक्रमा करेगा, मेरे सिंहासन की नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king with drummers and dance teachers, pointing to a scroll
panels.action: Bhagya Chandra sits with pung drummers and dance teachers, pointing to a palm-leaf manuscript, while a pung rests on the floor and a young boy demonstrates a martial step.

dialogue.text: Around 1779, tradition says, he turns his dream into discipline. With drummers and gurus, he shapes a new Ras Lila, drawing from Lai Haraoba, Pung Cholom and martial movement.

i18n.hi: लगभग १७७९ के आस-पास, कहा जाता है, वह अपने सपने को साधना बनाता है। ढोलियों और गुरुओं के साथ, वह नया रसलीला गढ़ता है, लाई हराओबा, पुंग चोलोम और युद्ध-नृत्य से रस लेकर।

panels.shot: gentle mid-shot of the king speaking to a young princess in ornate costume
panels.action: In the palace, Bhagya Chandra bends slightly to speak to his daughter Bimbamati, now dressed in elaborate Manipuri costume, her cylindrical skirt gleaming, as attendants adjust her ornaments.

dialogue.text: Sources agree: he places his daughter Bimbamati as Radha. Royal blood steps into the role of the soul, turning the Ras into both worship and royal statement.

i18n.hi: सभी स्रोत मानते हैं: वह अपनी बेटी बिंबामती को राधा बनाकर खड़ा करता है। रॉयल खून आत्मा की भूमिका में उतरता है, और रस, पूजा भी बनता है और राज-दावा भी।

panels.shot: wide, frontal shot of the first Ras Lila performance in a temple courtyard
panels.action: Under a full moon in the temple courtyard, dancers in layered Manipuri costumes move in a circle around the Govindaji idol; pung drummers play in the background, while Bhagya Chandra watches from a side platform.

dialogue.text: The Ras Lila rises: measured steps, curved hands, controlled spins. Old Meitei gestures now retell Vaishnava stories, turning the battlefield generation into a disciplined ring around Krishna.

i18n.hi: रसलीला उठती है: नापे कदम, मुड़ी उँगलियाँ, थामे हुए चक्कर। पुराने मैतेई हावभाव अब वैष्णव कथाएँ सुनाते हैं, जंग झेल चुकी पीढ़ी को कृष्ण के चारों ओर अनुशासित वृत में बदलते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of the king’s eyes reflecting the circling dancers
panels.action: A tight focus on Bhagya Chandra’s eyes shows the reflection of dancers circling Govindaji, a faint tear at the corner as the rhythmic movement continues.

dialogue.speaker: king_bhagya_chandra
dialogue.text: Let them remember this circle longer than they remember our wars.

i18n.hi: हमारी जंगों से ज्यादा, उन्हें इस घेरे की याद रहे।

panels.shot: wide shot of later generations performing Ras Lila, with a faded overlay of the king
panels.action: In a much later scene, children and adult dancers perform Ras Lila before the same Govindaji idol, while a translucent, dignified image of Bhagya Chandra watches from the background like a memory.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars trace manuscripts, temple practice and performance lineages. Beyond legend, they see a deliberate royal project: art as policy, devotion as a way to rebuild identity after exile.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान पांडुलिपियाँ, मंदिर-रीति और नृत्य-परम्परा की कड़ियाँ जोड़ते हैं। दंतकथाओं के पार वे एक सोचा-समझा राज-प्रयास देखते हैं: कला को नीति बनाना, और भक्ति को वनवास के बाद पहचान जोड़ने का रास्ता।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of Manipur valley with a Ras Lila pavilion glowing at night
panels.action: At night, the Imphal valley lies quiet under the stars while a Ras Lila pavilion glows softly in the distance, dancers just visible in silhouette, and a faint outline of Bhagya Chandra’s figure merges with the hills.

dialogue.text: Bhagya Chandra’s reign ends, but the Ras circle endures. In it, a small frontier kingdom still remembers how one exiled king turned loss into a living, moving theology around Govindaji.

i18n.hi: भाग्यचन्द्र का राज खत्म होता है, पर रस का घेरा बना रहता है। इसी घेरे में सीमा की यह छोटी रियासत अब भी याद रखती है कि एक वनवासी राजा ने कैसे हार को गोविंदजी के चारों ओर घूमती, जीवित, चलती फिरती थ्योलॉजी में बदल दिया।

subtitle_i18n.en: Exile, Vision, and the Birth of the Ras Lila
subtitle_i18n.hi: वनवास, दर्शन और रसलीला का जन्म
